summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a complex medical history including acute myeloid leukemia in remission after bone marrow transplant, anthracycline-induced cardiomyopathy with an ejection fraction of 10%, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, cryptogenic organizing pneumonia, and sarcoidosis, was readmitted due to recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection. He had been discharged recently after treatment for gastrointestinal symptoms but developed worsening diarrhea, prompting re-evaluation. Testing confirmed toxigenic C. difficile, and he was treated with oral vancomycin and intravenous metronidazole. Due to persistent symptoms, IV metronidazole was continued and later transitioned to oral therapy. His condition improved over the course of the admission, with resolution of diarrhea and stable vital signs. He was discharged on a prolonged vancomycin taper and oral metronidazole, with plans for outpatient follow-up in primary care and infectious disease. His heart and lung conditions remained stable, managed conservatively with oxygen and dialysis.
